column3: “All these” preserves the unspecific demonstrative rather than explicitly adding “the latter five.”
The fleeing kings remain the stated subject of “they fell there”; a separate subject “some men” is not expressed.
The subject is simply “they,” rather than explicitly “the four kings.”
The taking is followed by “and they went away,” before the final statement that Lot lived in Sodom.
“His brother” preserves the kinship image rendered “his relative.”
The action names “he and his servants” and then says that he struck and pursued them, without explicitly naming “Chedorlaomer’s army.”
“Lot his brother” preserves the kinship image rendered “his relative Lot.”
“And he was priest” preserves the coordinated statement rather than the causal “since he was priest.”
“He blessed him” retains a pronoun rather than explicitly naming Abram.
“He gave him” preserves the two pronouns rather than explicitly naming Abram and Melchizedek.
